items.what: Oleshky local ceasefire takes effect (03:00 Kyiv / 04:00 Moscow); main aid and evacuation mission on 29 Oct.
items.expected: Ukrainian and Russian General Staffs; the White House
items.happened: The local ceasefire took effect at 03:00 Kyiv time on 27 Oct and both sides say they are observing it; the aid and evacuation mission is due from 29 Oct ([ZN.ua](https://zn.ua/ukr/UKRAINE/v-okupovanikh-oleshkakh-pochav-dijati-rezhim-tishi-hotujut-humanitarnij-koridor-dlja-misiji-ta-evakuatsiji.html)).

items.what: Israeli Knesset election ([[e:2026 Israeli legislative election]]).
items.expected: Israel's Central Elections Committee; polls show neither bloc at 61 seats (Al Jazeera)
items.happened: Held 27 Oct. Final results gave Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats, Eisenkot's bloc 48 and Arab-led parties 19; Herzog opened consultations on 4 Nov. ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/5/israels-herzog-accepts-vote-results-opens-talks-on-forming-a-government))

items.what: Pezeshkian meets Putin at the gas exporters' (GECF) summit in Moscow.
items.expected: Iranian FM Araghchi and Iranian media (via AFP)
items.happened: Putin met Pezeshkian on 27 Oct on the sidelines of the GECF summit, citing 10.4% trade growth and continued work on Bushehr. ([Türkiye Today](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/region/putin-hosts-iranian-qatari-leaders-on-sidelines-of-moscow-gas-summit-3231155))

items.what: Trilateral US–Russia–Ukraine working-level talks in Abu Dhabi, 10–11 Nov. Russia's team is led by [[p:Vladimir Medinsky]], Ukraine's by [[p:Rustem Umerov]].
items.expected: Kremlin spokesman Peskov; Zelensky confirmed technical talks Update 26 Oct: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov says Moscow is ready to resume talks after 4 Nov. Update 5 Nov: US envoy Steve Witkoff set the dates as 10–11 Nov in Abu Dhabi (Kyiv Post).

items.what: Brazil runoff result: Lula vs Flávio Bolsonaro.
items.expected: Brazil's electoral court (TSE) releases results overnight; final Datafolha poll 51–49 for Flávio
items.happened: Lula won a fourth term with 51.79% to 48.21% (TSE official result); Flávio Bolsonaro refuses to concede and says he will seek annulment over a court-ordered voting extension. [TSE](https://www.tse.jus.br/comunicacao/noticias/2026/Outubro/presidente-do-tse-anuncia-reeleicao-de-lula-e-faz-balanco-do-2o-turno-das-eleicoes-2026)

items.what: Serbia snap election results.
items.expected: Serbia's electoral commission (RIK); Euronews says the outcome will be clear next week
items.happened: The Student List won about 52.5% with 96% counted (RIK preliminary), against 39.3% for Vučić's list, and Vučić conceded on election night. [Danas](https://www.danas.rs/vesti/politika/izbori26/rik-rezultati-izbora-izlaznost/)

items.what: Bulgaria presidential runoff, expected to be Iotova vs Gyurov.
items.expected: Trend polling agency (via euronews.bg); Sega
items.happened: Iotova won the 1 Nov runoff with about 57.6% to Gyurov's 39.5%, on low turnout (near-final count). ([Reuters via The Star](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2026/11/02/bulgaria039s-iotova-wins-presidential-runoff-near-final-results-show))

items.what: ECB rate decision; deposit rate widely expected to stay at 2.5%, with possible signals on France.
items.expected: ING's Carsten Brzeski (via Euronews)
items.happened: The ECB held its main rates on 29 Oct (deposit rate 2.5%); reports say Lagarde announced she will step down early. ([Investment Week](https://www.investmentweek.co.uk/news/4538092/ecb-holds-interest-rates-steady-lagarde-resigns-president))

items.what: US Federal Reserve rate decision.
items.expected: Prediction markets price about a 94% chance of a hold (DeFi Rate)
items.happened: The Fed held at 3.75–4.00% on 28 Oct in a 10–2 vote; Cook and Hammack dissented in favour of a hike. ([Admiral Markets](https://admiralmarkets.com/analytics/traders-blog/fomc-october-2026-fed-holds-rates))

items.what: Sweden: Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist reports to the Speaker; a new PM vote is possible late in the week.
items.expected: Fokus (Cecilia Garme)
items.happened: On Monday 26 Oct, Centre Party leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist reported to Speaker Andreas Norlén that there is a majority for centrist policy but no parliamentary support for a centre-led government, so the centrist option can be shelved. Norlén is consulting party representatives by phone and will announce the next step later; as of 27 Oct, no new mandate or PM vote date had been set, and SVT commentators expect Ulf Kristersson to be tasked next ([TV4](https://www.tv4.se/artikel/29NbTkqNw3aSYaGIoTWOEs/thand-ringqvist-c-har-laemnat-sin-rapport-foelj-saendningen-haer)).

items.what: EU gas storage reference date for the relaxed 80% fill target.
items.expected: EU gas storage regulation; IEEFA says the target is borderline
items.happened: EU storage stood at about 74.6% on 31 Oct and 74.1% on 3 Nov (GIE AGSI+ via Global Energy Flow), short of the relaxed 80% target and about 12 points below the five-year norm; Germany about 60.6%. [Global Energy Flow](https://global-energy-flow.com/storage/trajectory/)

items.what: Possible new US strikes on Iran.
items.expected: NIAC, CNN (US officials: operations possible within 96 hours of an order), Al Jazeera. A possible renewed US strike campaign on Iran after the 3 Nov US midterms. The White House has said there will be no attack before the vote, and a third carrier group is heading to the region.
items.happened: Yes, limited: US forces struck Qeshm Island on 2 Nov after the IRGC fired on a US aircraft, per US officials. After the midterms Trump said he had no immediate plans for more strikes. ([CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-negotiations-midterms/))

items.what: US midterm elections.
items.expected: Scheduled; forecasts favour Democrats in the House (Silver Bulletin average D+8.9)
items.happened: Democrats won the House and at least 54 Senate seats; Alaska and Mississippi were still uncalled on 5 Nov. ([CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/senate-election-results-2026/))

items.what: UN Security Council vote on renewing the MINURSO mission in Western Sahara (mandate expires 31 Oct).
items.expected: Morocco World News
items.happened: Both drafts failed on 30 Oct: Russia vetoed the US text (11–1–3) and Russia's rollover got only 3 votes. MINURSO's mandate lapsed and liquidation began on 1 Nov. ([Morocco World News](https://www.moroccoworldnews.com/2026/11/344641/western-sahara-un-begins-minurso-liquidation/))

items.what: Third Russia–Africa Summit in Moscow; Putin and AU chair Ndayishimiye co-chair the plenary on 29 Oct.
items.expected: TASS; Modern Diplomacy
items.happened: Held 28–29 Oct; participants adopted a 2027–29 joint action plan, and Putin backed a permanent African UNSC seat. ([Tchadinfos](https://tchadinfos.com/2026/10/30/sommet-russie-afrique-un-nouveau-plan-de-cooperation-adopte-jusquen-2029/))

items.what: Fifth Plenum of the CCP Central Committee, Beijing, 26–29 Oct.
items.expected: Tencent News; Newsquawk (no official Xinhua notice seen)
items.happened: The plenum (26–29 Oct) adopted a resolution on "full and rigorous" Party self-governance, confirmed the expulsions of senior officials including Zhang Youxia and Ma Xingrui, elevated Zhang Shengmin to the Politburo, and set the 21st Party Congress for the second half of 2027. ([CGTN communiqué](https://news.cgtn.com/news/2026-10-29/Communique-of-the-Fifth-Plenary-Session-of-20th-CPC-Central-Committee-1RDN23bl4ze/share_amp.html))

items.what: Thai no-confidence debate on PM Anutin; the government proposes a vote on 30 Oct, the opposition wants November.
items.expected: Thai PBS World
items.happened: No vote in October: whips agreed a censure debate on Anutin and 17 ministers for 7–10 December. ([Nation Thailand](https://www.nationthailand.com/news/40072840))

items.what: German President Steinmeier's state visit to China, 27–31 Oct.
items.expected: Chinese foreign ministry
items.happened: Steinmeier met Xi on 30 Oct; he said Xi saw no preparation for a US–China–Russia summit on Ukraine and insisted Europeans be at the table. ([ZDFheute](https://www.zdfheute.de/politik/ausland/steinmeier-china-russland-usa-gipfel-ukraine-100.html))

items.what: French union national mobilisation day.
items.expected: French unions (via Euronews)
items.happened: The 5 Nov strike went ahead: 575,000 marchers by Interior Ministry count, 1.6 million per the CGT, with 448 arrests. PM Lecornu called a 'social conference' with unions and employers for 9 Nov. [Business News (AFP)](https://businessnews.com.tn/2026/11/05/france-la-colere-gronde-jusqua-16-million-de-manifestants-dans-les-rues/1427419/)

items.what: APEC in Shenzhen; possible Trump–Xi–Putin meeting on nuclear arms and Ukraine.
items.expected: Reuters (via RTÉ); the Kremlin

items.what: European Council budget summit on the 2028–34 MFF.
items.expected: Agence Europe (26–27 Nov); Euronews (26 Nov)

items.what: First Russian diesel cargo under the US–Russia deal due in New York.
items.expected: Kpler (via Euronews)
items.happened: No delivery. By 5 Nov the two sanctioned tankers from Primorsk (Talisman and Leruo) had turned toward Brazil and the Mediterranean, and a third switched from New York to 'for orders' after New Jersey's governor told terminals to refuse the fuel. [AP via News4Jax](https://www.news4jax.com/business/2026/11/05/tankers-carrying-russian-diesel-change-course-raising-doubts-about-shipments-to-us/)

items.what: Rada vote on extending martial law and mobilisation to 29 Jan 2027 (bills 16182/16183).
items.expected: Due before the current terms expire on 31 Oct (Slovo i Dilo).
items.happened: The Rada voted on 26 Oct to extend martial law and mobilisation for 90 days from 31 Oct, to 29 Jan 2027 (281 votes for mobilisation). ([UNN](https://unn.ua/en/news/following-the-extension-of-martial-law-the-verkhovna-rada-extended-mobilization))

items.what: State Duma first reading of Russia's 2027–29 federal budget.
items.expected: Scheduled for 29 Oct; United Russia says it will back it (Vedomosti).
items.happened: The State Duma passed the 2027–29 federal budget at first reading. ([Vesti](https://www.vesti.ru/ns/gosduma-prinyala-proekt-byudzheta-na-2027-2029-gody-v-i-chtenii))

items.what: Gagauzia People's Assembly and Bashkan elections in Moldova.
items.expected: Set for 15 Nov (Moldovan media).

items.what: NATO consultations on letting pilots down radar-tracked drones without visual identification.
items.expected: Lithuanian PM Sinkevičius expects a rule change 'probably within a month' (LRT).

items.what: Pentagon recommendation on US force posture in Europe (possible drawdown of 25,000–40,000).
items.expected: Final recommendation due in November, per NBC reporting in September. Update 9 Nov: Elbridge Colby said in Bucharest (4 Nov) that Trump is expected to decide US force levels in Europe in early December (Romania Insider).

items.what: The Oleshky humanitarian mission (aid deliveries and evacuation) is due to start under the local ceasefire, which should hold until at least Saturday.
items.expected: Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets; AP
items.happened: Routes were demined on 29 Oct and buses evacuated residents from 30 Oct under the local truce; Melania Trump said nearly 800 people were evacuated before the truce ended. ([ITV](https://www.itv.com/news/2026-10-30/ukrainian-official-says-some-residents-have-been-evacuated-from-russia-occupied-oleshky), [UNN](https://unn.ua/en/amp/nearly-800-people-evacuated-as-part-of-the-mission-in-oleshky-melania-trump))

items.what: Sweden: Speaker Andreas Norlén is to announce the next step in government formation after the Centre Party's exploratory mission ended. Commentators expect Ulf Kristersson to get the next mandate.
items.expected: Norlén press release; SVT commentator Elisabeth Marmorstein
items.happened: Norlén put Centre leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist to a PM vote on 3 Nov; she was rejected 25–324. Moderate leader Ulf Kristersson now has a week to explore forming a government. ([Placera](https://placera.se/nyheter/thand-ringqvist-rostas-ned-i-riksdagen-2026-11-03))

items.what: Brazil: watch for PL/Bolsonaro requests at the TSE seeking removal of Lula's ticket for alleged abuse of power, and for any US measures after Trump called the vote rigged.
items.expected: ND Mais citing CNN campaign sources
items.happened: At least 22 abuse cases (15 citing Lula, 7 citing Flávio Bolsonaro) remain open at the TSE with no ruling date. ([TV Sim Brasil](https://tvsimbrasil.com.br/brasil/eleicoes-2026/noticia/2026/11/01/tse-mantem-22-acoes-contra-lula-flavio-apos-2-turno))

items.what: UN Security Council briefing on Iran non-proliferation, requested by Bahrain, Denmark, France, Latvia, the UK and the US, with [[p:Rafael Grossi]] briefing on Iran's denial of [[p:IAEA|International Atomic Energy Agency]] access since June. A procedural vote on the agenda may be held.
items.expected: Security Council Report (What's In Blue)
items.happened: Held on 27 Oct: IAEA chief Rafael Grossi told the Council the agency cannot verify Iran's roughly 440 kg of highly enriched uranium and asked for access to bombed sites; inspections continue only at Bushehr. [Shabtab News](https://english.shabtabnews.com/2026/10/28/grossi-urges-iran-to-grant-access-to-damaged-nuclear-sites/)

items.what: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority starts legal action against Sinokor vessels from 1 Nov. Watch for seizures or strikes on Korean-managed ships and Seoul's response.
items.expected: Iran International (PGSA statement)
items.happened: No seizure or strike on a Sinokor vessel was reported in the first days after 1 Nov; the warning stands while attacks on other shipping off Limah continued on 1 and 3 Nov. [Global Energy Flow Hormuz tracker](https://global-energy-flow.com/hormuz/)

items.what: [[e:2026 Israeli legislative election]]: exit polls at 22:00 on 27 Oct, then final results and the official publication of results, followed by President [[p:Isaac Herzog]]'s consultations with party delegations before he assigns the task of forming a government
items.expected: Central Elections Committee; President's Residence under the Basic Law timetable Update 5 Nov: results certified 4 Nov and consultations under way; Herzog has several days after them to name a nominee (Al Jazeera).
items.happened: Final results gave Netanyahu's bloc 53, Eisenkot's 48 and Arab-led parties 19; after consultations, Herzog gave [[p:Gadi Eisenkot]] the first mandate on 8 Nov, and the new Knesset is sworn in on 10 Nov ([Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/eisenkot-gets-nod-to-form-government-vows-unconventional-acts-in-time-of-emergency/)).

items.what: Turkish parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee on the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, a possible motion to deploy personnel to Saudi Arabia, and whether Riyadh requests Egyptian help under the new Egyptian mandate
items.expected: AKP MP to Reuters (motion after ratification); Al Jazeera on the Egyptian mandate
items.happened: Parliament ratified the Mecca pact on 4 Nov, 279–119. No separate deployment motion has been reported; the defence minister said the scope of support would be set later. No Saudi request for Egyptian help has been reported ([Al-Monitor](https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2026/11/turkeys-parliament-ratifies-mecca-pact-boost-saudi-arabia)).

items.what: Post-election push on the Gaza plan: [[p:Board of Peace]] and [[p:International Stabilization Force]] deployment, plus France's promised conference for the Lebanese army 'after' Israel's election
items.expected: Board of Peace official (ToI, 26 Oct); Macron (Asharq Al-Awsat)

items.what: House Democratic leadership elections, with [[p:Hakeem Jeffries]] running for Speaker; House Republicans also choose leaders after Mike Johnson stepped aside.
items.expected: House Democrats scheduled the vote for 18–19 Nov (CBS News)

items.what: Final calls in the uncalled Senate races in Alaska (Sullivan vs Peltola) and Mississippi (Hyde-Smith vs Colom).
items.expected: CBS News rates both toss-ups; Colom campaign says about 15,000 affidavit ballots remain

items.what: Canada–US trade agreement after the restart of talks.
items.expected: Mark Carney says teams will work toward a deal "over the coming weeks" (Al Jazeera)

items.what: Argentina: state workers' union ATE stoppage at 27 airports on 6 Nov, two days before Pope Leo XIV arrives; he visits Peru in mid-November.
items.expected: ATE (via Rio Times); EFE on the papal trip
items.happened: The 6 Nov airport stoppage did not happen: ATE suspended it on 5 Nov at the request of Argentina's bishops, promising to resume protests after the visit. [[p:Pope Leo XIV]] landed in Buenos Aires on 8 Nov and was met by [[p:Javier Milei]] ([Vatican News](https://www.vaticannews.va/en/pope/news/2026-11/pope-leo-xiv-arrival-argentina-welcome-ceremony-airport.html); [DataGremial](https://www.datagremial.com/informacion-general/ate-suspende-las-protestas-en-la-anac-por-la-visita-del-papa-y-una-llamado-al-dialogo-de-economia-202611516340)).

items.what: South Africa: official [[p:Electoral Commission of South Africa|IEC]] results of the 4 Nov local elections, then coalition talks in Johannesburg, Tshwane and eThekwini.
items.expected: The IEC says it will announce official results on Sunday 8 Nov.
items.happened: The IEC declared final results on 8 Nov: ANC 30.76% (its worst ever), DA 24.64%, MK 9.76%, EFF 6.22%, ActionSA 5.67%; only 74 of 213 councils have a majority, and coalition talks are starting in the Gauteng metros ([Mail & Guardian](https://mg.co.za/news/south-africa/2026-11-08-anc-barely-hangs-on-as-da-and-actionsa-make-gains-in-final-iec-results/)).

items.what: Mekelle: deadline for handing in unlicensed firearms, followed by house-to-house searches.
items.expected: Announced by the federal army (ENDF), reported by Wazema Radio: three days from the 7 Nov curfew.
items.happened: The army's surrender deadline for unlicensed firearms in Mekelle was reported as 8 Nov, with daytime house-to-house searches announced alongside a night curfew; no reporting yet on how the searches went. ([Critical Threats](https://www.criticalthreats.org/briefs/ethiopia-war-security-review/november-6-2026))

items.what: Georgia: the [[p:Constitutional Court of Georgia|Constitutional Court]] resumes hearings on [[p:Georgian Dream]]'s suit to ban five opposition parties.
items.expected: Court schedule, reported by Georgia Today: hearings resume 9 Nov after a one-week pause.
items.happened: The 9 Nov session did not take place: the court adjourned it because of a judge's health, with no new date announced ([Sova News](https://sovanews.tv/en/2026/11/08/court-hearing-on-banning-opposition-parties-in-georgia-postponed/amp/)).

items.what: Pakistan: [[p:Peshawar High Court]] hearing on PTI's challenge to emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
items.expected: Next hearing set for 10 Nov by the bench, reported by the Express Tribune and Samaa; PTI wants a larger bench.
items.happened: No hearing: on 7 Nov the court struck all petitions against the emergency and governor's rule off its cause list, citing Federal Constitutional Court directives; they cannot be heard until further orders ([Express Tribune](https://tribune.com.pk/story/2639251/phc-strikes-off-petitions-against-governors-rule)).

items.what: Armenia: publication of the draft new constitution, Azerbaijan's condition for signing the peace treaty.
items.expected: Justice Minister Srbuhi Galyan expects publication in November (Massis Post).

items.what: COP31 climate conference in Antalya, 9–20 Nov.
items.expected: UNFCCC/UNRIC schedule.

items.what: France: Lecornu's 'social conference' on wages on 9 Nov; Senate takes up the social-security budget 9–18 Nov.
items.expected: PM Lecornu (AFP); LCP for the Senate timetable.
items.happened: At the 9 Nov Matignon social conference Lecornu brought forward a 1.6% minimum-wage rise to 1 Dec (net €1,502/month), raised the overtime tax-exemption ceiling and widened the profit-sharing bonus, all to be added to the finance bill as amendments. ([Public Sénat](https://www.publicsenat.fr/actualites/politique/pouvoir-dachat-sebastien-lecornu-annonce-une-hausse-anticipee-du-smic-a-1-502-euros-des-le-1er-decembre))

items.what: Sweden: Kristersson reports back to the Speaker; the Centre Party wants answers from both blocs by 13 Nov.
items.expected: Speaker Andreas Norlén extended the mandate by "a few days" (Riksdag); Centre deadline per SVT.

items.what: Poland: Constitutional Tribunal judges' assembly on lifting Święczkowski's immunity and detaining him.
items.expected: Convened for 17 Nov by Anna Korwin-Piotrowska (PAP via PCh24).

items.what: Spain general election, 29 Nov.
items.expected: Called by PM Sánchez on 5 Oct; polls show a PP–Vox majority (Infobae).

items.what: UN Secretary-General race: next straw poll, possibly with colour-coded ballots showing permanent-member vetoes.
items.expected: Diplomats quoted by The National.

items.what: Serbia: new National Assembly convenes and the Student List names a PM; presidential election due by 27 Dec.
items.expected: Constitutional deadlines (Al Jazeera): assembly within 30 days of the 5 Nov final results.

items.what: UN Security Council emergency meeting on the Komyshuvakha strike, requested by Latvia (date not yet set).
items.expected: Latvian FM Baiba Braže (Censor.NET)

items.what: Whether any Russian diesel cargo is actually delivered to the US under the October arrangement.
items.expected: AP / Kpler tanker tracking

items.what: Whether Transnistrian leader [[p:Vadim Krasnoselsky]] returns from Moscow and how the five-year exit ban is applied.
items.expected: Moldova's Bureau for Reintegration Policy (NewsMaker)

items.what: Operation Carthage: anti-corruption court rulings on custody for the SBU and police suspects.
items.expected: NABU / SAP

items.what: State Duma second reading of Russia's 2027–29 budget.
items.expected: Vesti / State Duma schedule

items.what: Moldova's gas-shortage state of emergency expires; watch for an extension and the OSCE-facilitated Transnistria winter gas talks.
items.expected: AFP (via Al Jazeera)

items.what: OFAC licence for Lukoil foreign-asset sale talks expires; possible approval of the Boehly-led bid.
items.expected: Reuters (via Kyiv Post)

items.what: Belarus amnesty bill text: does it cover political prisoners?
items.expected: Lukashenko's press service (Zerkalo)

items.what: Israel: [[p:Gadi Eisenkot]]'s 28-day mandate to form a government ends (extendable by 14 days).
items.expected: Times of Israel / AP

items.what: Washington's reply to Iran's two-day plan and the Qatari-backed draft (day 1: blockade lifted and some funds released; day 2: Hormuz reopens, then nuclear talks).
items.expected: Gulf News and Al Jazeera say a US response is awaited after Trump met Qatar's PM on 9 Nov; Trump cites 'positive momentum'.

items.what: Iraq: whether more Iran border crossings close under the US Treasury request (Mandali closes temporarily from 13 Nov).
items.expected: Iraqi FM Fuad Hussein (Reuters) says talks with Washington continue; Border Ports Authority (INA) announced the Mandali closure.

items.what: Syria–Saudi defence coordination visits and whether Syria joins the [[e:Mecca defence pact|Mecca Joint Defence Agreement]]; confirmation of Syrian troop deployments.
items.expected: SANA's diplomatic source says coordination visits to Syria are planned next month and the deal could become a mutual defence pact.
